proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(N(v)=N_{C_G}(v)\) and \(N(H)=\bigcup_{u\in H}N(u)\).  Because \(\mathcal K\) is a vertex cover, \(V\setminus\mathcal K\) is edgeless.  If \(k=0\), then \(C_G\) itself is edgeless, so the greedy rule in \(\texttt{def:wri-law}\) selects every vertex for every strict priority order.  Consequently
\[
 F_{\ell,A}(z)=z^n
 \qquad (|A|\leq 2)
\]
by \(\texttt{def:tagged-count-polynomial}\).  This case takes polynomial output time and uses only integers.  Henceforth suppose \(k\geq1\).

Fix a rule \(\ell\), an independent set \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K\), and \(\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\mathcal U\).  Define
\[
 W_{\mathcal U}=(V\setminus\mathcal K)\cap N(\mathcal U),
 \qquad
 T_{\mathcal U}=(V\setminus\mathcal K)\setminus N(\mathcal U),
 \qquad
 S_{\mathcal U}=\mathcal U\cup T_{\mathcal U}.
\]
If a greedy output has intersection \(\mathcal U\) with the core, independence excludes every vertex in \(W_{\mathcal U}\).  Conversely, each vertex in \(T_{\mathcal U}\) must be selected.  Indeed, if \(v\in T_{\mathcal U}\) were unselected, \(\texttt{lem:greedy-domination-certificate}\) would provide a previously selected neighbor of \(v\); there is no such neighbor in \(\mathcal U\) by the definition of \(T_{\mathcal U}\), and there is no such neighbor in \(V\setminus\mathcal K\) because that set is edgeless.  Thus \(S_{\mathcal U}\) is the unique possible greedy output whose intersection with \(\mathcal K\) is \(\mathcal U\).  In particular, the contribution indexed by \(\mathcal U\) is zero unless \(A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}\).

The vertex-cover condition also makes every component of \(C_G-\mathcal K\) a singleton.  For an untagged \(v\in W_{\mathcal U}\), the selected message in \(\texttt{def:cutoff-forest-messages}\) is zero, while the singleton component factor is
\[
 \int_0^1 B_v(y,z)\,dy
 =\int_0^{p_v(x)}h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\,dy
 =p_v(x)^{h_{\ell v}},
 \qquad
 p_v(x)=\max_{u\in\mathcal U\cap N(v)}x_u.
\]
For \(v\in T_{\mathcal U}\), one has \(p_v(x)=0\).  Hence \(C_v(y,z)=h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\), \(B_v(y,z)=0\), and the component factor is
\[
 \int_0^1 A_v(y,z)\,dy
 =z\int_0^{r_v(x)}h_{\ell v}y^{h_{\ell v}-1}\,dy
 =z r_v(x)^{h_{\ell v}},
 \qquad
 r_v(x)=\min\bigl(\{x_f:f\in\mathcal B\cap N(v)\}\cup\{1\}\bigr).
\]
This formula is unchanged when \(v\) is tagged, because tagging sets \(B_v=C_v=0\).  If instead a tagged exterior vertex belongs to \(W_{\mathcal U}\), then \(A_v=0\) and tagging also sets \(B_v=C_v=0\), so its component factor is zero.  Combining this exterior-tag test with the core-tag condition in \(\texttt{def:core-inclusion-exclusion}\), and then invoking \(\texttt{prop:core-inclusion-exclusion}\), gives
\[
 F_{\ell,A}(z)
 =\sum_{\substack{\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K\text{ independent}\\ A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}}}
 z^{|S_{\mathcal U}|}
 \sum_{\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal K\setminus\mathcal U}
 (-1)^{|\mathcal B|} I_{\ell,\mathcal U,\mathcal B},                         \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
\begin{split}
 I_{\ell,\mathcal U,\mathcal B}
 ={}&\int_{(0,1)^{\mathcal K}}
 \chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(x)
 \prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}x_f^{h_{\ell f}-1}
 \prod_{v\in W_{\mathcal U}}
 \left(\max_{u\in\mathcal U\cap N(v)}x_u\right)^{h_{\ell v}}\\
 &\quad\cdot
 \prod_{v\in T_{\mathcal U}}
 \left(\min\bigl(\{x_f:f\in\mathcal B\cap N(v)\}\cup\{1\}\bigr)\right)^{h_{\ell v}}\,dx .       \tag{2}
\end{split}
\]
All exponents in (2) are nonnegative integers, because \(\texttt{def:feedback-core-input-class}\) requires \(1\leq h_{\ell i}\leq b\).

We now evaluate (2) without enumerating the \(k!\) chambers.  For \(f\in\mathcal K\), put
\[
 \operatorname{Pred}(f)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathcal U\cap N(f),&f\in\mathcal B,\\
 \varnothing,&f\notin\mathcal B,
 \end{cases}
\]
and, for every \(S\subseteq\mathcal K\), define
\[
\begin{split}
 E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S)={}&
 \sum_{f\in S}(h_{\ell f}-1)
 +\sum_{\substack{v\in W_{\mathcal U}\\
                    \mathcal U\cap N(v)\subseteq S}}h_{\ell v}
 +\sum_{\substack{v\in T_{\mathcal U}\\
                    \mathcal B\cap N(v)\cap S\neq\varnothing}}h_{\ell v}.                 \tag{3}
\end{split}
\]
This is a nonnegative integer.  Partition \((0,1)^{\mathcal K}\), apart from its tie set, into ascending chambers
\[
 0<x_{\sigma(1)}<\cdots<x_{\sigma(k)}<1.
\]
The tie set has probability zero because the densities in \(\texttt{def:wri-law}\) are continuous.  On such a chamber, \(\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(x)=1\) exactly when every member of \(\operatorname{Pred}(f)\) occurs before \(f\).  This is precisely the family of strict inequalities \(x_u<x_f\) in \(\texttt{def:core-inclusion-exclusion}\).

Let \(S_r=\{\sigma(1),\ldots,\sigma(r)\}\).  After removing the constant \(\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}\), the integrand in (2) is a monomial on the chamber.  Its total exponent on the coordinates in \(S_r\) is exactly \(E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S_r)\).  The density exponent \(h_{\ell f}-1\) is included exactly when \(f\in S_r\).  A maximum over \(\mathcal U\cap N(v)\) is the last of its arguments in the ascending order, so its exponent is included exactly when all its arguments are in \(S_r\).  A nonconstant minimum over \(\mathcal B\cap N(v)\) is the first of its arguments, so its exponent is included exactly when at least one argument is in \(S_r\).  These are the three terms of (3).

If the resulting chamber monomial is \(\prod_{j=1}^k x_{\sigma(j)}^{a_j}\), successive integration of the smallest remaining coordinate, using \(\int_0^t x^a\,dx=t^{a+1}/(a+1)\) for \(a\geq0\), gives
\[
 \int_{0<x_{\sigma(1)}<\cdots<x_{\sigma(k)}<1}
 \prod_{j=1}^k x_{\sigma(j)}^{a_j}\,dx
 =\prod_{r=1}^k
 \frac{1}{r+\sum_{j=1}^r a_j}
 =\prod_{r=1}^k\frac{1}{r+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S_r)}.                    \tag{4}
\]
Every division is valid because the denominator in the \(r\)-th factor is at least \(r\geq1\).

Define the entered-subset dynamic program by
\[
 D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[\varnothing]=1,
\]
and, for each \(S\subsetneq\mathcal K\) and \(f\in\mathcal K\setminus S\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Pred}(f)\subseteq S\), make the update
\[
 D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[S\cup\{f\}]
 \mathrel{+}=
 \frac{D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[S]}
 {|S|+1+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S\cup\{f\})}.                              \tag{5}
\]
Induction on \(|S|\) proves that \(D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[S]\) is the sum over all admissible ascending orderings of the elements of \(S\) of the product of the factors in (4) along their successive entered subsets.  The base case is the empty product.  For the induction step, the last entered element is some \(f\in S\), its predecessors must already lie in \(S\setminus\{f\}\), and the last factor is \((|S|+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S))^{-1}\), exactly as in (5).  At \(S=\mathcal K\), these admissible orderings are exactly the chambers where \(\chi_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}=1\).  Thus (2)--(5) imply the evaluated identity
\[
 I_{\ell,\mathcal U,\mathcal B}
 =\left(\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}\right)
 D_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}[\mathcal K].                                      \tag{6}
\]
Equations (1), (3), (5), and (6) therefore give every coefficient of every tagged polynomial by rational additions, multiplications, and divisions, with no remaining integral.

There are at most
\[
 \sum_{\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal K}2^{k-|\mathcal U|}=3^k
\]
disjoint pairs \((\mathcal U,\mathcal B)\); the independence test on \(\mathcal U\) only decreases this number.  For a fixed pair, tabulating (3) and all transitions (5) costs \(2^k\operatorname{poly}(n,k,\lambda)\) elementary operations.  Formula (1) contributes a single monomial for that pair and can be accumulated for the at most \(1+n+\binom n2\) tags satisfying \(A\subseteq S_{\mathcal U}\).  Across the \(L\) rules, the arithmetic-operation count is therefore \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\).

It remains to control exact bit cost.  Put \(D_0=nb\) and \(M=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,D_0)\).  A transition reaching a subset \(S\) of size \(r\geq1\) divides by
\[
 q(S)=r+E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S).
\]
The sets \(W_{\mathcal U}\) and \(T_{\mathcal U}\) partition \(V\setminus\mathcal K\).  Hence (3), \(h_{\ell i}\leq b\), and \(r\leq k\) give
\[
 1\leq q(S)
 \leq r+r(b-1)+(n-k)b
 =rb+(n-k)b
 \leq nb=D_0.                                                                 \tag{7}
\]
Thus \(q(S)\mid M\).  Store every layer-\(r\) dynamic-program value over the common denominator \(M^r\); an update from layer \(r-1\) multiplies the old numerator by the integer \(M/q(S)\).  There are at most \(r!\) paths to a layer-\(r\) state, and every factor in (4) is at most one, so the stored numerator has absolute value at most \(r!M^r\).  Moreover,
\[
 \log_2 M\leq\log_2(D_0!)\leq D_0\log_2 D_0.                                 \tag{8}
\]
After multiplication by \(\prod_{f\in\mathcal K}h_{\ell f}\), accumulation of at most \(3^k\) signed terms over denominator \(M^k\) increases numerator bit length by at most \(O(k\log b+k\log k+k+k\log M)\).  Equations (7)--(8), together with \(k\leq n\), bound the bit length of every numerator and denominator by \(\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\).  The integer \(M\) can itself be formed by successive greatest-common-divisor and least-common-multiple operations within this bound.  Standard exact integer arithmetic therefore makes the bit cost of each of the \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) arithmetic steps polynomial in \(n,b,\lambda\), and this polynomial factor is absorbed in the displayed bound.

For an exact smallest-instance check, let \(n=2\), \(\mathcal K=\{f\}\), and let the exterior vertex \(v\) be adjacent to \(f\).  Equations (1)--(6) give
\[
 \Pr_{\ell}(S_{\ell}=\{f\})
 =\Pr(X_{\ell f}>X_{\ell v})
 =\int_0^1h_{\ell f}x^{h_{\ell f}-1}x^{h_{\ell v}}\,dx
 =\frac{h_{\ell f}}{h_{\ell f}+h_{\ell v}},
\]
and the complementary probability for \(S_{\ell}=\{v\}\).  Therefore
\[
 F_{\ell,\varnothing}(z)=z,
 \quad
 F_{\ell,\{f\}}(z)=\frac{zh_{\ell f}}{h_{\ell f}+h_{\ell v}},
 \quad
 F_{\ell,\{v\}}(z)=\frac{zh_{\ell v}}{h_{\ell f}+h_{\ell v}},
 \quad
 F_{\ell,\{f,v\}}(z)=0,
\]
which exhausts all admissible tags.  At the opposite boundary \(k=n\), the exterior sums in (3) vanish and every denominator in (7) remains positive, so the proof does not require a nonempty exterior.

If the supplied \(\mathcal K\) is a vertex cover of \(C_G\), then all \(F_{\ell,A}(z)\), \(|A|\le2\), are computable exactly in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations, with no unevaluated integral, and every intermediate rational has \(\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit length.

This narrows the previously advertised resource envelope from factorial chamber enumeration to the proved \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit bound and proves polynomial, rather than merely fixed-parameter, intermediate rational height.

proposed.gap: Static vertex-cover programs do not assign heterogeneous greedy-order probability.
proposed.consumer: Experiments whose measured conflict cycles are concentrated on a small vertex-cover hub set obtain an exact fixed-parameter AWRI rule comparison.

prose_updates.tldr: Weighted random isolation creates exposure-compatible focal units under network interference, but published AWRI rule selection relies on simulation. Conditioning on a supplied size-\(k\) feedback vertex set and applying a three-state forest recursion with \(3^k\) core inclusion--exclusion yields an exact, fully evaluated dense algorithm for every zero-, one-, and two-tagged isolated-count law in \(Ln^2k!3^k(nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) bit operations. The tagged laws reconstruct every dense RDIM risk matrix. Rational weak semidefinite optimization then returns an independently checkable \(\varepsilon\)-minimax certificate in time polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and the binary encoding length of \(\varepsilon\); for canonical \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\), this dependence is polynomial in \(p=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\). When the supplied core is a vertex cover, an entered-subset cumulative-exponent dynamic program evaluates every admissible chamber implicitly and computes all tagged laws, with no unevaluated integral, in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations with polynomial intermediate rational bit length. An evaluated recurrence also covers identical replicated-star attachments, but fixed-parameter closure for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments remains open.

project_justification.gap: AWRI fixes the weighted greedy design and balanced RDIM estimator but simulates a surrogate. Random sequential adsorption treats scalar occupation, while structural graph programs count static sets. General semidefinite design methods neither supply the exact WRI/RDIM risk matrices nor give an end-to-end rational certificate with complexity measured against the binary encoding of an arbitrary rational tolerance. None of these results gives the evaluated heterogeneous tagged integration used here. The entered-subset dynamic program closes the vertex-cover special case, without an integration gate, in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations, but arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments still lack a fixed-parameter representation.
project_justification.niche: A supplied feedback set exposes a forest decomposition on which exact heterogeneous priority integration is possible. The proved general guarantee is XP in the feedback size. If the supplied core is a vertex cover, every exterior component is a singleton and the cumulative priority exponent is determined by the subset of core coordinates already entered; this yields an \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) dynamic program with polynomial rational height. Identical attachment profiles give a second evaluated special regime. Once the exact rational risk library is available, the finite ellipsoidal risk game admits a rational primal-dual certificate whose computation is polynomial in the encoded tolerance; for dyadic tolerance \(2^{-p}\), it is polynomial in \(p\).
project_justification.fill: The paper proves core inclusion--exclusion, a fully evaluated dense chamber-polynomial algorithm with controlled rational bit height, exact tagged RDIM risk reconstruction, and a rational near-minimax certificate. In the vertex-cover subclass, it replaces factorial chamber enumeration by an entered-subset recurrence, obtaining all tagged laws exactly and without unevaluated integrals in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations with polynomial intermediate rational height. The certificate algorithm is polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and the binary encoding length of \(\varepsilon\), specializing to polynomial dependence on \(p=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\) for canonical dyadic input \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\). The paper records arbitrary-forest fixed-parameter moment closure as an open problem rather than assuming it.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li supply the published directed-network FNI/TTE/WRI plus balanced-RDIM causal-design construction used here. This note first identifies WRI deletion with greedy maximal-independent-set selection on the neighborhood-overlap conflict graph, and then proves exact algorithms only for the positive-integer-weight subclass with a supplied feedback set. Positive rational priority weights transfer by multiplying all exponential, equivalently Beta, rates by a common denominator, which preserves their random order; arbitrary published real weights are not covered by the exact Turing-model algorithms. Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li derive a balance and inverse-size MSE surrogate and use simulation for candidate-weight selection. Pippenger's random-sequential-adsorption recursions, Gamarnik and Goldberg's rooted-tree bonus recursions, and the local-limit equations of Krivelevich, Meszaros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman do not compute exact finite heterogeneous tagged moments. Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li count static independent sets on bounded-treewidth graphs, and Borie, Parker, and Tovey give finite-state decomposition methods, but neither weights maximal independent sets by heterogeneous priority orders. Cygan, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk, and Wojtaszczyk establish a \(2^{O(k\log k)}\) scale for a different feedback-set problem, not an oracle for the present integration. The present \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) vertex-cover bound instead comes from a problem-specific entered-subset dynamic program for cumulative cutoff exponents; it contains no unevaluated integral and does not settle heterogeneous forest closure. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje study an unrestricted network-experiment minimax functional; no equality with that functional is claimed. Kallus motivates mixed minimax design, and Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong develop semidefinite minimax-design methods. Boyd and Vandenberghe supply the finite-dimensional separating-hyperplane theorem and its open-set converse used in the minimax interchange. Groetschel, Lovasz, and Schrijver's Theorem 4.3.13 supplies weak constrained convex minimization for centered convex bodies given by weak-membership and convex-function value oracles; the rational affine-SDP parametrization, radius bounds, membership tests, and pullback needed here are proved separately in this note. Aronow and Samii provide the design-based interference framework. Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet motivate the rural-China insurance application but provide no evidence that its measured conflict graph has small feedback number or a small vertex cover.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact algorithm removes Monte Carlo error from comparison of prespecified WRI rules, but its worst-case general cost is XP rather than fixed-parameter in the feedback number. If a measured conflict graph comes with a small vertex-cover core, the entered-subset cumulative-exponent program gives exact tagged-law computation, with no integration gate, in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations and with polynomial intermediate rational bit length. Identical repeated attachments admit a separate evaluated recurrence. Neither special case establishes fixed-parameter tractability for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments. The final semidefinite certificate concerns worst-case squared error of the fixed RDIM rule library over the stated endpoint ellipsoid; it is not a claim of optimality among all network designs or estimators.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The dense chamber-polynomial representation closes arbitrary heterogeneous branching, component products, moving endpoints, and tags, but uses \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\) states. It therefore proves an evaluated XP theorem, not the originally proposed fixed-parameter theorem. In the vertex-cover case, every exterior component is a singleton, so the entered core subset \(S\subseteq\mathcal K\) determines the scalar cumulative exponent \(E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S)\); this is exactly why the \(2^k\)-state recurrence closes. Branching forest components instead retain distinct future ordered-ratio exponent profiles. Two heterogeneous branches can have the same present activation count and exponent while leaving different exponents on future variables. The unresolved question is whether a shared operator representation can preserve those profiles in \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) time. A table indexed by \(k\) degree totals, a profile-count vector with an \(n\)-dependent exponent, or a circuit retaining an integration gate does not solve that question.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The general proved result assumes a supplied feedback set, positive integer priority weights, and permits XP dependence \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\); it neither finds a minimum feedback set nor proves arbitrary-feedback-set fixed-parameter tractability. The exact \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) guarantee, absence of an unevaluated integral, and polynomial rational height require that the supplied feedback core also be a vertex cover; the other evaluated special result concerns the stated identical replicated-star coefficient. Nondegenerate isolation is required only for RDIM denominators and risk reconstruction. The minimax result chooses within a prespecified WRI/RDIM library over a graph-Sobolev endpoint ellipsoid and does not equal the unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax functional. The rural-China follow-up is a prospective consumer, not evidence for a small empirical feedback number, a small vertex cover, a calibrated ellipsoid, or improved field performance.

statement_notes.justification: The entered-subset cumulative-exponent dynamic program sums every admissible core-order chamber without factorial enumeration, yielding the exact \(6^k\) fixed-parameter oracle, no unevaluated integral, and polynomial intermediate rational height.
